object: Sainte-Chapelle upper chapel, west-facing interior with the Rose of the Apocalypse
creator: Medieval builders and artists; individual authors of all visible fabric not established here
work_date: Main chapel built 1241–1248; west rose rebuilt around 1485; later restoration also present
branch: French Gothic interior: Rayonnant enclosure with a later Flamboyant west rose
rights_evidence: The exact Commons file page/API identifies Dudva, 12 February 2023 and CC BY-SA 4.0.
attribution: Dudva, Interior of Saint-Chapelle in Paris.jpg, 12 February 2023, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. Public provider thumbnail; no local retouch or crop.
claim_scope: A readable Gothic spatial comparator for linked ribs, slender window divisions and high glazed enclosure. The later west rose is a Flamboyant Gothic component, not an unchanged thirteenth-century Rayonnant window.
observable_features: Pointed vault ribs repeat from bay to bay and continue toward slender vertical members beside tall stained-glass fields.
Glazing occupies most upper wall fields, while narrow structural-looking strips articulate the vertical rhythm.
A large circular rose with branching curved tracery organizes the far wall above a narrower horizontal gallery/entrance zone.
The roof stars and gold accents remain subordinate to the legible rib, bay and window hierarchy; no visitors or temporary display elements obstruct this upward view.
limits: An upward west-facing view, not a complete room survey or exact measurement. This present interior contains thirteenth-century spatial fabric, a west rose rebuilt around 1485 and later restorations. The image does not establish the date of every panel or paint layer, original color calibration, structural performance or generic Gothic identity from one pointed arch.

association_evidence.supports: The exact Commons file identifies the Saint-Chapelle interior, photographer Dudva, capture date and photo license.
The monument describes its thirteenth-century Rayonnant stone/glass system and explicitly distinguishes the later western rose.
The monument identifies the current west rose as Flamboyant Gothic, rebuilt around 1485 under Charles VIII. This date applies to that component, not all visible fabric.
